content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Solve equations with unknowns on both sides
contains an unknown (usually $x$) raised to the power of 1.
an equation means finding the value of the unknown that makes the equation true.
Explore equation solving — practise solving linear equations step by step using the interactive visualisation below.
Think of an equation as a balance scale. Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other to keep it balanced.
[DIAGRAM: Balance scale showing 3x + 5 = 14, then 3x = 9 after subtracting 5 from both sides]
Do the same operation to both sides.
Use inverse operations in reverse order (undo the last operation first).
Collect the unknowns on one side and numbers on the other.
Move the smaller $x$ term to avoid negative coefficients.
Equations with Negative Terms on Both Sides
do the same to both sides
collect $x$ terms on one side, numbers on the other
multiply by the denominator or find a common denominator
